transcript:
Header: 2025-09-16 15:30 UTC | Duration: 42m | Recording ID: ff-20250916-hr-0347
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood Security), Lena (Harbor CISO), Marco (Harbor Infra), Priya (Harbor Compliance)

Summary: Short SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture review covering reports, Trust Center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, KMS/encryption, and data residency. Agreed to share artifacts and schedule a technical deep dive.

00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, with Ethan and Ravi from our security and infra team.
00:15 - Lena: Hi, Lena here. We've been evaluating Redwood for inference across our retail analytics pipelines; main thing for us is the compliance posture.
00:30 - Ethan: Great, thanks. We'll run through our SOC 2 and ISO 27001 coverage, how you can access artifacts, and then Ravi will go deeper on KMS, audit logs, RBAC.
00:45 - Marco: Just to set expectations, we have some strict data residency needs and a preference for VPC/private deployment for PII PII-ish workloads.
01:05 - Ravi: Totally understood. We support Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment options. For Private we provide a customer-managed control plane and can support on-prem options.
01:25 - Priya: Can you send the SOC 2 report? We need the Type II report and the controls mapping spreadsheet to map to our internal matrix.
01:40 - Maya: Yep, we'll send SOC 2 Type II and ISO cert. We'll also include a controls mapping CSV that maps Redwood controls to common frameworks.
01:55 - Priya: Awesome. Also: Trust Center access — can we get a viewer account? We don't want to share prod creds.
02:10 - Ethan: Yes, we have a Trust Center with role-based access. We can create a temporary viewer role for you. Note: names may be Redwood Console or 'Trust Center' depending on export.
02:30 - Marco: On the technical side, can you describe audit log retention and what you log? We need chain of custody for request metadata and K V cache events and also admin actions.
02:50 - Ravi: We retain audit logs for X months by default — (note: transcription may have placeholders) — but we can configure retention with enterprise add-ons. Logs include session start/end, API keys usage, user identity via SAML/SSO, changes to RBAC, and model rollout events.
03:15 - Marco: Do you capture full request/response payloads in logs? That's a big ask for us.
03:30 - Ethan: By default we log metadata and hashes for content; full request/response payload logging is configurable but not default for hosted. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can support more flexible logging policies and even route logs to your SIEM (via syslog or forwarder).
03:55 - Lena: KMS — we want BYOK and HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest. What's supported?
04:10 - Ravi: We support cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and have an upcoming HSM integration path. For Private deployments we offer customer-managed KMS where you hold the keys and Redwood encrypts with envelope encryption. There may be a short onboarding for key rotation policies.
04:35 - Priya: Does Redwood support CMEK or only service-managed keys?
04:45 - Maya: We support CMEK patterns for Dedicated and Private; hosted can use customer keys for certain artifacts but we should follow up with the exact matrix in the controls doc.
05:05 - Marco: Data residency — can you pin data to a single region and prevent cross-region replication?
05:20 - Ethan: Yes, customers can specify region pins for storage and processing. For hosted, we have regional clusters; for Dedicated/Private you run in your VPC region. We'll capture your residency requirements in the mapping.
05:40 - Lena: For ISO 27001, will you share scope and the certificate? We need to confirm which services are in-scope.
05:55 - Ravi: We'll share the ISO 27001 certificate and the statement of applicability. It will show which services are in-scope (serving runtime, control plane) and any exclusions.
06:15 - Priya: We also need evidence of controls: change management, patching cadence, vulnerability scans, pen tests, and supplier management.
06:30 - Maya: We can include SOC 2 and ISO evidence packages — typically redacted reports and supplementary artifacts. We'll provide the SOC 2 Type II and ISO cert and a controls mapping that references evidence IDs.
06:50 - Marco: Regarding SSO, do you support SAML and SCIM provisioning? We want automatic user provisioning and group sync to map to RBAC roles.
07:05 - Ethan: Yes, SAML S S O is supported plus SCIM provisioning for user sync. RBAC is role-based with custom roles; you can map groups to roles and enforce least privilege.
07:30 - Lena: Any third-party sub-processors or hosting partners we should be aware of?
07:40 - Ravi: We list subprocessors in the Trust Center; primary compute partners are major cloud providers for hosted. For Dedicated/Private customers you can eliminate some subprocessors if you run in your VPC or on-prem.
08:00 - Priya: Can you explain the controls mapping format? We need a row-per-control with Redwood control ID, description, evidence pointer, and correspondence to SOC/ISO control IDs.
08:15 - Maya: Yep that's the format we'll send — CSV with columns for control_id, description, framework_mapping, evidence_link, last_tested_date. We'll also include short notes on any compensating controls.
08:35 - Marco: For network segmentation, do you allow private peering and customer-managed security groups?
08:50 - Ethan: Yes, for Private we support V P C peering and customer-managed security groups and route tables. We can consult on subnet design and NAT vs private endpoints.
09:10 - Lena: How do you handle model rollout auditing — like who can deploy which model and how do we restrict access to higher-capacity endpoints?
09:30 - Ravi: Model rollouts are tied to RBAC. You can have an operations role for deployments and limit higher-capacity endpoints to specific teams. Rollouts have audit entries and can be canaryed.
09:50 - Priya: About retention of logs for legal holds — can you retain logs beyond standard retention?
10:05 - Ethan: Yes, with enterprise add-ons we can increase retention and provide export to your archival storage. We'll note retention SLAs in the follow-up doc.
10:25 - Marco: Anything about pen testing windows — do you allow customers to run auth tests or simulated attacks?
10:40 - Ravi: We coordinate pentests; customers should request a window and we provide a scope and point of contact. Some restrictions apply for hosted shared infra, but Dedicated/Private is more flexible.
11:00 - Lena: Who signs the DPA and can we get SLAs in the contract for availability and incident response?
11:15 - Maya: Yes DPAs are standard; for Dedicated/Private we have SLA add-ons with incident response and support tiers. We'll attach standard DPA and propose SLA language if needed.
11:35 - Priya: A question on encryption in transit — do you support mTLS between your services and customer endpoints?
11:50 - Ethan: We support TLS 1.2+ and mutual TLS for Private deployments; hosted supports TLS with mutual authentication options for some integrations.
12:10 - Marco: Are there any known gaps between your SOC 2 controls and ISO mapping we should watch for?
12:25 - Ravi: There's always nuance. We'll call out gaps in the controls mapping doc. For example, some physical security controls may differ in scope if you run on a public cloud. We'll annotate compensating controls.
12:45 - Maya: We'll put those gap notes in the CSV and include recommended mitigations and any timeline for remediation.
13:05 - Priya: For audit logs, can we get a sample export format? JSON lines or CSV?
13:20 - Ethan: We support JSON-lines and can export via S3 bucket delivery or push to a SIEM connector. We'll include a sample in the follow-up.
13:40 - Lena: Is the Trust Center a self-serve portal with checklists? We're used to Okta style portals that list controls and evidence.
13:55 - Maya: Yes, Trust Center has docs, subprocessor list, certs, and ability to request artifact access. We'll create a viewer link for you.
14:15 - Marco: One more network question — do you support private link endpoints to avoid public internet egress?
14:30 - Ethan: Yes, PrivateLink and private endpoints are supported in Dedicated/Private. Hosted may offer private connection options via partner networking.
14:50 - Priya: For KMS rotation policies, how often are keys rotated and do you provide rotation logs?
15:05 - Ravi: Rotation can be configured per your KMS provider; Redwood logs key usage and rotation events and includes them in audit logs. We'll document the default rotation cadence and how to enforce your own.
15:30 - (crosstalk) Maya: Okay, let's summarize next steps...
15:40 - Maya: Action items — I'll send SOC 2 and ISO certs and the controls mapping spreadsheet; Ravi will prep KMS notes; Ethan will schedule the technical deep dive with Marco.
16:00 - Priya: We'll send over our residency matrix and any contractual clauses we require.
16:15 - Lena: Timeline — we aim to complete vendor security review in two weeks and start pilot by mid-October.
16:30 - Maya: That timeline seems doable. We'll try to get artifacts to you by tomorrow and get the deep dive on calendar for next week.
16:45 - Marco: Thanks everyone. One small note — please obfuscate any customer names in shared evidence.
17:00 - Ravi: We'll redact customer-specific content in shared artifacts.
17:15 - Maya: Great. We'll follow up with the Trust Center link and the files.
17:30 - Priya: Thanks, bye.
17:40 - (call ends)

Recap: Agreed deliverables: SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 certificate, controls mapping CSV with evidence pointers, Trust Center viewer access, sample audit log export, KMS integration notes, and calendar invite for a technical deep dive.

References/Links Mentioned: Trust Center (will share link), Controls mapping template (CSV), SOC 2 Type II report (attached in follow-up), ISO 27001 certificate (attached in follow-up).

Note: Transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., 'V P C' for VPC, 'K V cache' for KV cache).
